Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MediTech Innovations Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; John Ramirez, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Mike Thompson, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. MediTech Innovations achieved record results this third quarter, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance. First, our hospital and ambulatory surgery center adoption rates. Second, our strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter. Third, overall performance highlights and key achievements. Fourth, competitive dynamics and market share trends. Fifth, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains. Sixth, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary. Seventh, inventory management and working capital optimization. And eighth, capital equipment versus consumables mix trends.

John will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Elena will update us on our technology advancements, and Mike will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

Now, let's get started with our hospital and ambulatory surgery center—or ASC—adoption rates, which continue to be a cornerstone of our growth story here at MediTech Innovations. Our portfolio, anchored by the PrecisionNav robotic navigation platform and our suite of minimally invasive orthopedic implants like the FlexiLock spinal fixation system, is uniquely positioned to capitalize on the shift toward value-based care, outpatient procedures, and higher OR throughput. Overall adoption of our PrecisionNav systems reached 28% penetration across our target addressable market of U.S. and EU hospitals and ASCs with annual ortho/neuro case volumes exceeding 500 procedures—that's up from 22% last year, driven by an 18% year-over-year increase in our global installed base to 2,450 systems. Utilization rates, measured as procedures per system per quarter, hit a record high of 142, which is 12% above our internal model, reflecting sticky recurring revenue from disposables that now account for 68% of segment sales at an average selling price of $2,450 per case.

Breaking it down by channel, hospitals represent 72% of our adoption revenue, where we saw robust but measured growth. Our hospital installed base grew 14% year-over-year to 1,780 systems, with penetration in top-tier integrated delivery networks—like those similar to Mayo Clinic and Vizient GPO members—climbing to 52%. A key driver was our Q3 launch of PrecisionNav 4.0 software, which integrates AI-driven haptic feedback and real-time 3D fluoroscopy fusion, reducing procedure times by 22% on average for total knee arthroplasties and anterior cervical discectomies. This has resonated amid staffing shortages and the push for bundled payments under CMS's ASCERT model. Hospital procedure volumes on our systems rose 16% year-over-year to 185,000 cases, with ASPs holding firm at $1.8 million per capital sale thanks to outcomes-based pricing contracts that now cover 45% of new hospital deals, sharing upside from reduced readmissions.

In contrast, ASCs are seeing explosive momentum. ASC adoption surged 32% year-over-year, expanding our footprint to 670 systems and capturing 19% market share in freestanding ASCs performing more than 200 ortho cases annually—up from 12% last year. This outpaces the broader ASC ortho market, projected at a 24% CAGR through 2028 by iData Research. Reimbursement tailwinds are significant: CMS's 2024 OPPS final rule boosted APC payments for robotic-assisted TKAs by 7.2% to $12,450, making our systems economically viable at scale. We've seen ASC chains like Surgery Partners and United Surgical Partners International standardize on PrecisionNav, with 15 new site-of-care expansions in Q3 alone. Utilization here is outstanding at 168 procedures per system quarterly, fueled by our ASC-optimized FlexiLock implants that cut OR turnover from 45 to 28 minutes. As a result, ASC channel revenue jumped 41% year-over-year to $285 million, with disposables ASPs at $2,100—our highest margin mix.

The trends are clear: migration of high-acuity procedures from inpatient to outpatient settings, with ASCs now handling 31% of all Medicare TKAs, up from 25% in 2022 per CMS data. Our PrecisionNav-enabled ASCs achieve 15% higher case volumes per OR versus legacy navigation like Brainlab's Curve, thanks to our cloud-based analytics dashboard that optimizes scheduling and predicts instrument wear. Macro headwinds like inflation haven't slowed us; our value proposition shines as hospitals face 4-6% OR cost inflation while ASCs operate at 20-30% lower overhead.

Regionally, the U.S. is our powerhouse at 76% of adoption revenue, with hospital penetration steady at 48% but ASCs leaping to 24%. California and Florida ASC markets are hotspots, where state-level site-neutral payment reforms accelerated shifts—our Florida installed base doubled to 120 systems. In Europe, adoption grew 22% year-over-year, led by Germany's DRG revisions favoring robotics; we hit 18% penetration in DACH hospitals and inked a landmark deal with Fresenius Helios for 45 ASC rollouts. UK NHS trusts are slower due to procurement cycles, but our NICE-compliant outcomes data on reduced length of stay—1.2 days versus 2.8 for manual procedures—is gaining traction. Asia-Pacific is nascent but promising with 9% year-over-year growth to 110 systems, primarily in private chains like Apollo Hospitals in India and Raffles Medical in Singapore. China remains gated by NMPA approvals, but our Phase III data submission for PrecisionNav could unlock a $1.2 billion total addressable market by 2026.

Strategically, we're pulling every lever. We've deployed over 1,200 surgeon training modules via our Virtual OR simulator, boosting adoption velocity by 27%, similar to Intuitive Surgical's early da Vinci approach but tailored for ortho/neuro. Partnerships expanded, including co-development with Johnson & Johnson Vision for integrated phacoemulsification add-ons targeting ophthalmic ASCs. Capital efficiency via our leasing program, now 52% of placements, lowers barriers with $1.2 million entry points versus $1.8 million outright buys, improving days sales outstanding to 52 days. Looking ahead, we expect ASC adoption to drive 25-30% of incremental growth in FY25, with hospital refresh cycles adding tailwinds as 30% of our base hits end-of-life.

Now, let's talk about our strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter, Q4 FY24. As we wrap up a strong Q3 with 14% year-over-year revenue growth to $1.42 billion—driven by 22% expansion in our structural heart franchise and resilient performance in orthopedics amid softer elective procedure volumes—our playbook centers on three pillars: accelerating innovation in high-growth adjacencies, optimizing our global footprint for margin expansion, and fortifying operational resilience in a dynamic macroeconomic and regulatory environment.

Priority one: advancing our innovation pipeline with key milestones in robotics and cardiovascular devices. In robotics, our PrecisionNav Xi platform—our single-port system competitive with da Vinci—is on track for full U.S. commercial rollout following FDA 510(k) clearance in late Q3. We've secured initial orders from 15 premier centers, including partnerships akin to Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic, expecting over 500 implants by quarter-end and ramping to 20% market share in ambulatory surgery centers by FY26. Utilization rates are at 85% post-install, with procedure times 15% faster than legacy systems, translating to $25 million in Q4 revenue from consumables.

In cardiovascular, we're prioritizing our next-gen TAVR valve, EchoFlow Ultra, which showed 95% one-year durability in our pivotal PERSEVERE trial—outperforming Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3 in hemodynamic performance. Pending final CMS reimbursement codes, we'll launch in 200 U.S. sites mid-quarter, targeting 18% year-over-year growth in structural heart to $450 million. Internationally, CE Mark expansion into Japan and India will add $50 million upside, capitalizing on Asia's 12% CAGR in TAVR adoption from aging demographics.

R&D investment will hit 9.5% of sales in Q4, up from 8.7% last year, with $120 million allocated to AI-enhanced imaging for our neuromodulation portfolio. Early data from our INSIGHT trial shows our dorsal root ganglion stimulator reducing chronic pain by 65% versus 50% for Medtronic's Intellis, positioning us for Q1 FY25 label expansion.

Priority two: regional expansion and market share gains in high-growth geographies. The U.S. remains core at 55% of revenue, but we're shifting mix toward emerging markets, which grew 28% in Q3 to 15% of total sales. In APAC, we'll double down on China post-NMPA approval for our knee implant system, aiming for 25% penetration in Tier-1 hospitals via partnerships like our WuXi AppTec collaboration, supporting $180 million in Q4 revenue fueled by China's orthopedics market expanding at 15% from urbanization-driven osteoarthritis.

Europe, at 20% of mix, faces German DRG reimbursement cuts, but our value-based care bundles—integrating AngioJet thrombectomy with telehealth—have driven 10% ASP uplift. We'll launch in 10 new countries, targeting 12% growth to $240 million. In Latin America and MENA, supply chain localization via our new Monterrey, Mexico facility will mitigate 20% tariff risks and support 30% year-over-year growth.

Priority three: driving margin expansion through operational excellence and supply chain fortification. Margins are top focus amid inflation and FX volatility. Q3 gross margins hit 68.5%, up 210 basis points year-over-year, thanks to 15% productivity gains in our Galway, Ireland plant via Six Sigma. For Q4, we guide to 69-70% through supply chain resilience—diversifying resins with 18-month contracts from three Asian suppliers, reducing lead times 25% and shielding Red Sea disruptions; inventory days stable at 120 with no stockouts. Cost discipline with SG&A to 28% of sales from 29.5% via zero-based budgeting and AI-driven sales force optimization—Salesforce Einstein boosted rep productivity 18%. Sustainability initiatives align with EU MDR and SEC climate rules, targeting 20% Scope 3 emissions cuts by 2026, enhancing ESG appeal.

Overall, these priorities underpin Q4 revenue guidance of $1.45-1.48 billion, implying 11-14% organic growth, with adjusted EPS of $1.45-1.50. We're confident in our 8-10% full-year algorithm, outpacing industry's 6% consensus per Evaluate MedTech. Risks include procedure deferrals from U.S. election uncertainty and biosimilar erosion, but our 45% recurring revenue mix provides a moat.

Moving on to overall performance highlights and key achievements for Q3 FY24. As a leader in cardiovascular, neuromodulation, orthopedics, and robotics, we've delivered another standout quarter in a market growing at 6-8% CAGR globally, fueled by atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and aging demographics projected to drive $150 billion in structural heart sales by 2030.

Top-line: total revenue $1.42 billion, up 18% reported and 16% constant currency—ahead of guidance and street consensus of 12-14%. Ninth straight double-digit growth quarter, outpacing Medtronic and Boston Scientific's mid-teens. By segment: structural heart, anchored by EchoValve Pro TAVR at 28% U.S. share per Millennium Research, grew 22% to $620 million on 35% U.S. procedure surge post low-risk indication. Electrophysiology $410 million, up 25%, via AI RhythmSync mapping for 20% faster AFib ablations, gaining 5 share points on Biosense Webster. Neuromodulation $280 million, up 14%, with spinal cord stimulator implants up 18% on BurstDR therapy under expanded CMS codes. Peripheral and capital $140 million, up 8%, resilient in drug-eluting balloons.

Profitability: gross margins 68.5%, up 210 bps from Galway efficiencies at 95% utilization and premium mix. Adjusted operating margins 28.2%, non-GAAP EPS $1.72 up 22% above $1.65 guide. Free cash flow $450 million or 31% of revenue, funding $300 million repurchases and 12% dividend hike.

Key achievements: FDA approval for EchoValve Pro Gen 2 with tissue-in-growth cuff reducing leaks to under 2% at one year—PIVOTALE trial in NEJM. Positions for 20-25% U.S. penetration by FY26. CE Mark for Symplicity Spyral RF renal denervation, timing with RDN market post-SPIRIT-OF. CardioCloud platform integrates Apple Watch/Fitbit ECG for 500,000 patients, up 40%, with neural networks cutting readmissions 18% in ACOs, generating $99 subscription revenue.

U.S. 62% sales up 20% on procedural demand, 2024 IPPS TAVR adjustments. EMEA 12% growth navigating Germany pricing via UK NHS value contracts. APAC 25% to 22% revenue, China JV 50,000 EchoValve implants, Japan JSR for RhythmSync eyeing 30% EP share.

Validates "Innovate, Acquire, Optimize": $750 million NeuroStim Dynamics tuck-in for ultrasound neuromodulation hedging opioids. Supply chain derisked 85% components dual-sourced Mexico/Vietnam vs Red Sea. Sustainability: 45% recyclable packaging, Newsweek Green list.

Fortifies raised FY24 guidance: revenue $5.85-$5.95 billion (17-19% growth), EPS $6.75-$6.85 in $120 billion market with 15 pipeline assets, $2.5 billion war chest.

Next, competitive dynamics and market share trends, validating our innovation strategy in a $620 billion market by 2027 at 5.4% CAGR per IQVIA, shaped by procedural recovery, value-based care, and competition in structural heart, neuromodulation, robotics.

Q3 global share 7.8% across franchises, up 90 bps from 6.9%, 11th straight gain on 12% unit growth, premium mix like AetherFlex TAVR/NeuroPulse, 2.1% ASP expansion. Outpaced 4.8% market organically via outcomes, surgeon adoption.

Cardiovascular (42% revenue): gaining on Boston Scientific/Edwards in structural heart; AetherFlex 14% U.S. TAVR share from 8% on 28% lower leak rates in ORBIT-3, 15% higher repeat share. Edwards ~45% leader, but we close gap in APAC to 11% from 6% via Japan KOLs, CE Mark 14Fr. CRM: PulseGuard ICD 9.2% U.S. share up 150 bps vs Medtronic Micra/Abbott Aveir, 22% mix to dual-chamber S-ICD, Apple ECG collab ahead of Biotronik.

Orthopedics/robotics: 5.4% in RoboGuide navigation vs Stryker/Zimmer; 18% robotic knee growth outpacing Intuitive 13%. Interoperable with da Vinci/Hugo, 25% hybrid OR Europe share. Counter Chinese OEMs like MicroPort low ASPs with Suzhou manufacturing cutting duties 12%, resilient vs Red Sea.

U.S. 58% revenue, 12.1% share up 310 bps on CMS TAVR-Y90, J-codes. Europe 22% sales 6.7% share via DGMP, DiGital OR AI. APAC 14% growth 4.2% share from 3.1%, NMPA AetherFlex challenges Terumo, 22% radial sheaths.

$1.2 billion R&D (12% sales): bioresorbable stents vs Boston Synergy targeting 20% 2026; AI Vantage imaging SaMD; $450 million NeuroDyno for 8% pain share vs Nevro. Outcome contracts 35% U.S. deals tie to readmissions.

Sustained tailwinds aging demographics 6-8% volumes, offset EU MDR delays. Goal 100+ bps FY24 to 8.5% global via 4,200 patents, #1 NPS.

Then, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains, foundational to margin expansion. Peers like Stryker/Intuitive/Boston run 28-35%; we deleveraged 320 bps to 28.2% Q3 from 31.4%, $48 million savings contributing 60% to 24.7% operating margin.

Selling (65% SG&A): field productivity 112% quota vs 98%, Salesforce Einstein territory realign 15% U.S. ortho/cardio, 22% less overlap, $2.8 million rev/rep up 14%. Predictive surgeon volumes cut calls 18%. MedTech Connect portal 68% KOL adoption, 25% less detailing; post-IDN consolidation (Kaiser/HCA 42% volume), 35% promo to digital 3.2x ROI.

G&A (35%): $22 million savings global shared services, SAP S/4HANA Phase 2 EMEA/APAC automating 75% invoices RPA, 40% faster procurement, 12% better $1.2 billion indirect terms on packaging/logistics vs resin/Red Sea volatility.

U.S. 52% rev 29.1% SG&A down 410 bps post ortho slowdown right-size 2,800 sales. EMEA 24% rev 26.8% down 520 bps Nordic Dublin hub MDR scale vs Smith+Nephew. Emerging 18% rev 32% flat on 22% cardio growth via India/Brazil JVs.

Reinvest 45% savings ($22 million) AccuNav spine robotics $4.5 billion TAM vs Globus; 30% digital therapeutics AI planning vs FDA SaMD. Expect 200-250 bps FY24 deleverage to sub-27% Phase 3 ERP/AI, $0.28 EPS from Q3, resilient vs COVID/inflation under CMS APC.

Next, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary. Q3 consolidated 68.5%, up 230 bps YoY from 66.2%, 110 bps sequential; sixth straight expansion, T4Q 67.8% above 65-68% target. Adjusted 69.2% ex inventory write-downs legacy EP catheters, leverage high-growth franchises.

Drivers: 150 bps mix to premium structural heart >75% margins—InnoFlow TAVR/MitraClip-like 28% growth vs 12% segment, U.S. volumes/Japan Shonin; commodity ortho down vs Asian comps. 80 bps pricing: U.S. 2-3% neuromod leads/IPGs accepted GPOs inflation; Europe 1-2% NHS/GKV offset value contracts AI monitoring 15% outcomes PROMETHEUS. 100 bps COGS: polycarbonate down 8% QoQ; $18 million manuf opt, yields 92-96% Singapore wearables; robotic stents labor -22%.

Supply chain: 99.2% on-time vs pre-pandemic, ahead Boston Sci. Headwinds Red Sea 15% freight, titanium 14 weeks, semis U.S.-China/TSMC.

Mitigations: dual/triple-source 85% components, silicone Dow alts, single-source <8% BOM. $250 million Reynosa Mexico 75% util local 40% heart prod, -30% leads like Stryker. Digital twins Siemens NX 12 plants, EtO -18% FDA emissions; IBM blockchain 5,000 tier-2 visibility DuPont fluoro.

Regions: NA 71% EP tailwinds; EMEA 65% MDR $45 million hip re-reg Ireland local; APAC 67% China 35% growth Mindray 10% synergies.

Q4 guide 68.5-69.5%, FY24 68.0-68.5% +200 bps. Risks tariffs/resin oil; $500 million buffer, 70% 2025 forwards. 70% 2026 robotics/bioresorbables.

Then, inventory management and working capital optimization, driving FCF. Q3 DIO -12 days YoY to 82 from 94, T12M turns 4.5x vs 3.9x/industry 4.1x MedTech Europe; inv/rev 18.2% -220 bps, $145 million WC free. CCC 65 days best 5yrs, DSO 58 stable, DPO 115 supplier neg.

Since 2022 $28 million Resilience Init: AI forecast SAP ML Epic OR/TAVR/BioFlex data, top 20 SKUs 78-92% acc, safety -15% no stockouts flu/surgery. SKU rational ABC sunset 18% low-vel laparo <35% margins, 4,200-3,450 items, obs reserve -40% $12 million like Intuitive.

VMI DuPont/Carpenter consignment DCs, DPO 90 days; EOQ FDA 21 CFR batch cardiac catheters vs 7% matl infl.

U.S. 52% rev DIO 75 consignment Kaiser/HCA NeuroStim JIT 8% vol OR backlogs. Europe 28% 95 MDR Galway -22 days transatlantic vs Boston. APAC 15% 70 dual China/India hedge geo, 12% CAGR min inv aging, ring IP EchoGuide.

Tailwinds value-based Medicare ASC single-use; sustainability bioresorb stents 30% recycled rare earths ESG. FY24 -10 DIO blockchain IBM CCC<60 $200 million FCF; fuel 15% R&D AI robotic endoluminal $650 billion 2028 Grand View.

Finally, capital equipment versus consumables mix trends, cornerstone high-margin recurring model. Cap equip like Horizon robotics/EchoFlex imaging drives base; consumables PrecisionGuide catheters/EndoShield scopes/BioFlux kits annuity 75-80% vs 45-55% cap.

Q3 $1.42 billion +14% rep +16% cc. Consumables 72% $1.02 billion +18% YoY 20% org, 5th double-digit on 12% util 4,200 Horizon base 28 proc/sys/mo vs 25. Cap 28% $400 million +6% disciplined capex post-COVID.

T12M consumables +400 bps 68-72%, gross 68.5% high 3yrs faster than Stryker/Medtronic 60-65% ortho/neuro. 5yr 55% single-use FDA sterile.

U.S. 52% rev 76% mix +500 bps ASC Horizon x2 hospital, PrecisionGuide ASP $1,450 value OR +25%. EMEA 24% 68% NHS capex Siemens EchoFlex +15% attach Benelux. APAC 18% +25% YoY 70% China BioFlux tenders aging 300m>60 India PLI 40% catheter local.

Tech: Gen-3 Horizon AI nav 85% attach vs 75% FlexTips -98% contam; $250 million smart IoT CardioFlow SaaS post-implant; BioFlux +22% RSV/flu. Dual Mexico/Vietnam polymer de-risk.

Optimize 15-18% base high-util urology/gyn <18mo payback; MedLease $200 million Q3. FY consumables 74-75% Q4 29 proc seasonal. Risks US tariffs 100-200 bps 80% hedge.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez for a review of our financial results.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter, with revenue of $1.42 billion up 18% year-over-year, gross margins at 68.5%, and adjusted EPS of $1.72. Expenses were well-controlled, with SG&A deleveraging to 28.2% and operating margins expanding to 28.2%. Free cash flow was robust at $450 million. For FY24, we're raising guidance to revenue of $5.85 to $5.95 billion and EPS $6.75 to $6.85. Q4 outlook is revenue $1.45 to $1.48 billion, EPS $1.45 to $1.50.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, John. We are excited about the progress we are making in our technology roadmap. Our latest innovation, PrecisionNav 5.0, is poised to transform orthopedic and neuro navigation with advanced AI haptics and 3D fusion. We expect FDA approval in Q4.

Our R&D pipeline includes next-gen TAVR EchoFlow Ultra, neuromodulation stimulators outperforming peers, and robotics expansions. Investments at 9.5% of sales are yielding breakthroughs like AI imaging and bioresorbables, positioning us for leadership in a $120 billion market.

Next, Mike Thompson with some insights on our commercial strategy.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Elena. We are focused on driving commercial excellence and expanding our global reach. Our strategic partnerships, like those with J&J Vision, Siemens, and regional JVs, are enabling access to new markets and segments. U.S. ASC growth, Europe value bundles, and APAC localizations are key, with sales force AI optimization boosting productivity. We're targeting 15-20% share gains in high-growth areas through leasing, training, and outcomes contracts.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Mike. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee - JPMorgan:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the ASC adoption surge to 32% growth, can you elaborate on the drivers beyond reimbursement and how sustainable is the 41% revenue jump?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, David. The surge is multifaceted: CMS OPPS boosts make economics compelling, but our PrecisionNav 4.0's 22% procedure time cuts and cloud analytics for 15% higher OR volumes are key differentiators. Chains like Surgery Partners standardizing, plus our leasing dropping entry to $1.2 million, accelerates velocity. Utilization at 168 procs/system shows stickiness. Sustainable as ASCs take 31% Medicare TKAs, riding 24% market CAGR—we see ASCs driving 25-30% incremental FY25 growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen - Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. Regarding gross margin expansion to 68.5% and supply chain, how are you viewing risks from Red Sea and potential tariffs into FY25?

John Ramirez:
Lisa, solid progress there. Mix shift to 72% consumables/high-margin structural heart gave 150 bps, pricing 80 bps despite Europe pressure, COGS 100 bps from yields and resin stabilization. Supply chain 99.2% OTD via dual-sourcing 85%, Mexico nearshoring 40% production, digital twins/IBM blockchain. Red Sea hit 15% freight but mitigated; tariffs risk via hedging 70% materials, $500 million buffer. Guide FY24 68-68.5%, on path to 70% 2026.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel - Morgan Stanley:
Hi team. Competitive share gains to 7.8%—thoughts on Stryker/Intuitive in robotics and Edwards in TAVR, plus China OEM pressure?

Mike Thompson:
Raj, our 90 bps gain is outcomes-driven: AetherFlex 14% TAVR share on leak reductions, interoperable RoboGuide 18% knee growth vs Intuitive 13%. China OEMs low ASP but we localize Suzhou cutting duties 12%, partnerships build moat. Edwards lead but we gain APAC/Japan; NPS #1 sustains surgeon loyalty. $1.2 billion R&D bioresorbables/AI keeps us ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Wong - Barclays:
Thanks. Impressive DIO to 82 days—details on AI forecasting impact and emerging market execution?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Emily, our AI SAP/Epic integration hit 92% accuracy top SKUs, -15% safety stock; SKU sunset 18% low-vel, VMI upstream risk. U.S. 75 days consignment IDNs, Europe 95 mitigated Galway, APAC 70 dual-source. Frees $145 million WC, CCC 65; FY24 another 10 days to $200 million FCF, fueling R&D like endoluminal robotics.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver sustainable growth.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
